champion.name: dualtrend
champion.hypothesis: Two trend-following ledgers: USDT side buys strength and sells for USDT profit; BTC side sells weakness and buys back for BTC profit. Gains net of fees and tax; trailing floors; hard stop.

lastEvaluation.diagnosis: The champion 180d run underperforms both benchmarks: strategy USD return +12.45% vs buy&hold +26.2% and static 50/50 +13.1%, and BTC-denominated equity is actually -10.9% (lost BTC). Fees are modest (3.69 USD over 180d, ~0.37% of capital; weekly fee/profit ratio ~14%), so fee drag alone doesn't explain the gap. The real drag is the BTC-side ledger: realisedBtcProfitUsd = -35.44 while realisedUsdtProfit = +29.28 — the USDT side is doing its job, but BTC-side shorts are net losers, wiping out the gain. openLots shows trackB=4 out of 4 open lots (100% of current inventory is stuck "against entry" track B), with unrealisedUsd -1.6, i.e. capital parked in adverse positions rather than compounding. hardStop is set at 0.422 (near the top of its [0.02,0.6] range), so a track-B lot can travel 42% against entry before stopping — with 2 hardStops firing in 180d this alone plausibly accounts for most of the -35 USD BTC-side loss. Compounding this, regime flips are frequent and short-lived: 5 grid<->moon flips inside a single week despite confirmBars=48/regimeDwellBars=144, and freefall regime occupies 20.1% of the 180d sample — the BTC side keeps selling into weakness per design during freefall, but rapid regime reversals mean it's repeatedly caught short into V-shaped bounces, feeding lots into track B where the loose hardStop then bleeds them. So the primary cost is risk-sizing on track B exits (hardStop too loose) amplified by false/short regime flips, not fee drag or tilt mis-sizing (tilt score 0.614 vs target 0.623 is well-tracked, endBtcShare 0.64 is reasonable given the trend).
hypotheses: Tightening hardStop and the ratchet floor on track-B lots will cut the -35 USD BTC-side realized loss and shrink the 100%-track-B parked inventory without materially reducing USDT-side gains.

Slower regime confirmation plus an ADX regime filter will suppress the observed rapid grid<->moon whipsaws (5 flips/week, 20% freefall share) and reduce false BTC-side entries into freefall, improving BTC-denominated equity at the cost of trade frequency; this is the more conservative, tighter-gating variant.
